scheduled_maintenances.name: The Datadog US1 Status Page Is Changing on October 29 2026.

incident_updates.body:
Datadog’s US1 status page is changing. Starting on October 29 2026, we’ll have a whole new look and experience based on Datadog’s own Status Pages product: https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/status_pages/ 

The new Datadog status page will be accessible via the same URL: https://status.datadoghq.com/. If you need to access the old version, you can find it at 1k6wzpspjf99.statuspage.io

The old status page will remain available, and Datadog will publish identical updates to both.

Notifications will continue to be delivered to all existing subscribers.
- Email notifications: On October 29, we will migrate all email subscriptions to the new status page. No action is required, and you will continue receiving email notifications as usual. Going forward, notifications will be sent from no-reply@dtdg.co.
- Slack: Notifications via the old Slack integration will continue to be delivered until further notice. On October 29, we recommend upgrading to the Datadog Slack app to take advantage of the latest features (https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/status_pages/#subscribe-in-slack)
- RSS Feed: RSS feeds will continue normally. 
- SMS and Webhooks: Your existing subscriptions to SMS messages and webhooks will continue to be delivered. 

If you typically view the Datadog status page via the web or supported subscription methods, no action is required. 

Custom integrations, workflows, and scripts that depend on the old status page url, structure, or API payloads may be affected by this transition. We recommend reviewing any custom integrations or code you have that pull data from Datadog’s status page. If you have custom integrations or code, you’ll need to take one of the following actions:

Change the URL in your custom integration or code to point to the old version 
Update your custom integration or code to consume our new status page structure or payloads

If you have any questions, please respond to this email or reach out to our support team by visiting help.datadoghq.com.

incident_updates.body:
With the end of Daylight Saving Time (DST) approaching at the end of the month you may need to upgrade or restart your Agents to fix an issue with DST handling in versions of the Agent older than 5.5.2.

# How do I know if I’ll be impacted?

You may ignore this message if:
     - Your server(s) clocks are set to UTC
     - You operate in a time-zone without daylight saving
     - Your server(s) are running agents greater than or equal to 5.5.2

# How to test if your server(s) are on UTC or DST

Linux or Unix: If you are using Linux/Unix, simply run "date" on your servers and if the output is something along the lines of "Sat Oct 29 22:00:56 UTC 2016", your servers are not affected. If they read something like "Sat Oct 29 18:09:09 EDT 2016" they are affected. 

Windows: Simply look at the time in the taskbar.

# How can I fix this?

If you are going to be affected there are 3 options you may take to avoid gaps in data and spurious alerts:
    1. We implemented a fix in version 5.5.2 - released on 26 OCT 2015 - to address this, the simplest way to avoid problems if your server(s) run in DST is to upgrade the Agent to a recent version before DST ends.
    2. If your server(s) clock is set to DST, you should upgrade the Agent to a version newer than 5.5.2 before DST ends (Nov. 6th in the US) 
or plan to restart the Agent right after DST ends to avoid seeing delays of 1 hour in your graphs at that time and receiving spurious "no-data" alerts.
    3. If the server(s) clock is set to DST (instead of UTC), the Agent will collect but not send metrics on Sunday, 6 NOV 2016 early morning, when DST ends, for 1 hour.

As a result you may see:
     - Missing data in your graphs for that one hour 
     - Spurious alerts due to Agents not reporting. 

If you cannot upgrade in time please plan to restart the Agent shortly after the daylight saving change.
If you have any questions or concerns please don’t hesitate to reach out to us at support@datadoghq.com - sorry for the inconvenience.

If your servers' clock are set to UTC or to a timezone without DST, you can ignore this message.

We recently discovered an issue that affects Datadog Agents only on servers with clocks set to Daylight Saving Time (DST). If your servers' clock are set to DST, you should upgrade the Agent to v5.5.2 before DST ends or restart the Agent shortly after DST ends. DST ends November 1st 2015, 2AM local time.

Impact of the DST bug
If the server's clock is set to DST (instead of UTC), the Agent will stop sending metrics for up to one hour after DST ends, or until it is is restarted. In the United States for instance, this is happening this Sunday (November 1st 2015, 2AM local time).

In practice this means that the agent will collect metrics but won't report for up to one hour after DST ends. If the agent is restarted in this hour, it will resume reporting normally.

If you have monitors on metrics with timeframes shorter than 1 hour, you may receive spurious alerts coming from the affected Agents.

How to tell whether your servers are affected
If you are using Linux/Unix, simply run "date" on your servers. If they read "Sat Oct 31 22:00:56 UTC 2015", your servers is not affected. If they read something like "Sat Oct 31 18:09:09 EDT 2015" they are affected.
On Windows, simply look at the time in the task bar.

What you can do to avoid the DST bug
You have 2 options:
* Schedule an agent restart shortly after DST ends (e.g. use cron or similar to restart the agent at 01:01 local time)
* Upgrade the Agents on the affected servers to 5.5.2, directions may be found here: https://app.datadoghq.com/account/settings#agent

Changelog for Agent 5.5.2: https://github.com/DataDog/dd-agent/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#552--10-26-2015

If you have any questions or concerns please don’t hesitate to reach out to us at support@datadoghq.com - sorry for the inconvenience.
